title: Understand speech recognition · Level 1
slo: Explain how speech recognition turns spoken input into text and identify common uses.

exercises.question_text: Which model converts audio into phonemes?

options.rationale: The acoustic model converts audio into phonemes. Phonemes represent specific sounds.
The language model maps phonemes to words. It works after sound representations exist.
options.better_fit: This fits mapping phonemes to recognized words.

feedback.intrinsic: Audio would not be converted into sound representations.
feedback.instructional: The acoustic model handles audio-to-phoneme conversion.

options.rationale: A speech synthesizer produces audio from text. It does not interpret incoming audio.
options.better_fit: This fits creating audible speech from written text.

feedback.intrinsic: Incoming speech would not be prepared for transcription.
feedback.instructional: This question concerns recognition, not synthesis.

options.rationale: A recognizer is the broader transcription capability. The acoustic model has the specific audio-to-phoneme role.
options.better_fit: This fits naming the overall transcription capability.

feedback.intrinsic: The precise model role remains unknown.
feedback.instructional: Separate the recognizer from the acoustic model.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The acoustic model handles audio-to-phoneme conversion.

exercises.question_text: Which are common uses of AI speech? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Clinicians can speak notes and have them converted to text. This reduces manual typing.
Contact centers can transcribe calls in real time. Transcripts support review and analysis.
Learning apps can listen to learners and provide pronunciation feedback. This supports spoken-language practice.
Transcripts support review and analysis. They do not replace all review work.
options.better_fit: This would fit an unrealistic claim that no human review is needed.

feedback.intrinsic: Staff would still need to review information.
feedback.instructional: Call transcription supports review; it does not replace it.

exercises.explanation: Correct. These are common uses in healthcare, support, and education.

exercises.question_text: A language model maps recognized words back into phonemes.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The word-mapping direction would be reversed.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The acoustic model produces phonemes; the language model maps them to words.

exercises.explanation: Correct. A language model maps phonemes to words, not words back into phonemes.

exercises.question_text: Customer-support call transcription can make conversations easier to review and analyze for sentiment.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Staff would have less convenient material for analysis.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Transcripts support conversation review and sentiment analysis.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Call transcripts can support review and sentiment analysis.

exercises.question_text: What do AI speech capabilities enable?

options.rationale: AI speech capabilities support interaction through spoken language. They can handle spoken instructions, questions, and captions.
Written-only interaction omits spoken language. AI speech capabilities are designed to support voice-related interaction.
options.better_fit: This fits an application designed exclusively for typed input and written output.

feedback.intrinsic: Users would still need to type.

options.rationale: Speech-to-text is one AI speech capability. The broader category includes other voice interactions too.
options.better_fit: This fits a transcription task that only converts speech to text.

feedback.instructional: Speech recognition is only one AI speech capability.

options.rationale: Text-to-speech is one AI speech capability. It does not interpret spoken input.
options.better_fit: This fits an app that reads written messages aloud.

feedback.intrinsic: Spoken instructions could not be understood.

exercises.explanation: Correct. AI speech enables voice-based interaction with software.

exercises.question_text: What does speech recognition do? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Speech recognition begins with spoken input. It detects what a person says.
Recognition interprets speech rather than merely storing sound. This supports usable output.
Recognized words become data, usually text. Applications can use that data.
Vocalizing written text is text-to-speech. Speech recognition moves from speech to text.
options.better_fit: This fits reading a written message aloud.

feedback.intrinsic: A caller's words would not become text.
feedback.instructional: Recognition handles input; synthesis produces output.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Recognition detects, interprets, and converts speech to data.

exercises.question_text: Voice interfaces can improve accessibility and inclusiveness, but they cannot feel natural for users.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This misses a user benefit of voice interaction.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Voice-based interaction can be natural and can improve access.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Voice interaction can feel natural while improving accessibility and inclusiveness.

exercises.question_text: What does Azure Speech in Microsoft Foundry Tools provide?

options.rationale: Azure Speech provides all three capabilities. They cover transcription, spoken output, and translation.
Speech-to-text is included but is not the only capability. Azure Speech also provides synthesis and translation.
options.better_fit: This fits an application that only needs transcription.

feedback.intrinsic: Spoken replies and translation would be missing.
feedback.instructional: Azure Speech includes STT, TTS, and translation.

options.rationale: Text-to-speech is included but Azure Speech does more. It also supports transcription and translation.
options.better_fit: This fits an application that only reads content aloud.

feedback.instructional: TTS is only one Azure Speech capability.

options.rationale: Custom voice creation is a supported task, not the full capability set. Azure Speech also supports recognition, synthesis, and translation.
options.better_fit: This fits a project focused specifically on custom voice creation.

feedback.intrinsic: Other speech capabilities would be overlooked.
feedback.instructional: Custom voices are one Azure Speech task.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Azure Speech provides speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and speech translation.

exercises.question_text: Speech recognition converts spoken words into data, usually text.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A transcript requires data from spoken words.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Speech-to-text converts interpreted spoken input into data, usually text.

exercises.explanation: Correct. This is the core purpose of speech recognition.

exercises.question_text: Azure Speech supports both prebuilt and custom Speech service models.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A team might wrongly assume every model must be built from scratch.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Azure Speech supports both prebuilt and custom models.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Azure Speech supports prebuilt and custom models for speech tasks.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the parts to form a correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The relationship between recognition and an app response is unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with the app, then state what recognition creates and its source.

exercises.correct_answer: An app can respond after recognition creates text data from speech
exercises.explanation: Recognition creates text data from speech, which an app can use to respond.

exercises.question_text: Azure Speech supports ___, the capability that determines who is speaking in a conversation.

parts.text: , the capability that determines who is speaking in a conversation.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A broad capability name would not identify this task.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use speaker identification for identifying speakers.

exercises.explanation: Speaker identification is the task of identifying speakers in a conversation.

flashcards.back: It converts spoken input into data, usually text.

flashcards.front: What does an acoustic model do?
flashcards.back: It converts audio into phonemes, or sound representations.

flashcards.front: What does a language model do?
flashcards.back: It maps phonemes to words and recognized text.
A service for speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and speech translation.
